newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade, dealers said on Friday.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. March existing homes sales data, which are forecast to be around 4.14 million annualised units compared with 4.26 million units reported in February.

"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning on some position adjustments and weekend booksquaring. Some people are waiting for tonight's release of the existing home sales figures, for more clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
"But unless the numbers are way off expectations, I don't think there will be much impact as most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent. Monday/Tuesday and week-fixed were unchanged from Thursday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent. Three-months rose 1/16 point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent, nine-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/4 6-1/8 and twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 6-7/16 6-5/16 percent.
